Subject: FW: Northvale RFP — draft answers + asks (internal)

Team — draft answers attached (Redwood_Northvale_HIPAA_RFI_answers_v1.pdf). Highlights / talking points to review before we send:

- BAA: Redwood will sign a standard BAA for customers that process PHI. We have an editable BAA; Marissa/Legal please prepare redline suggestions.
- Data handling: Hosted API does not use customer prompts to train our public models by default. Customers needing PHI processing should use Dedicated or Private (VPC / on‑prem) — those modes keep data within the customer's tenancy and do not feed back to model training.
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest. Customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM supported for Dedicated + Private.
- Logging & audit: Token-level request/response logging is configurable; audit logs (control plane events, access logs) are available and can be exported to customer SIEM (syslog/S3). Default retention = 90 days; retention can be contractually extended up to multi-year (per account agreement).
- Subprocessors: Primary compute and storage are provided by AWS (us-east-1) and GCP (us-east-1) depending on region; full list is in the appendix.
- Certifications & testing: SOC 2 Type II (report excerpt attached), annual external penetration testing — summary results available in Appendix-Technical-Evidence.zip.

Open items for this RFI (please action):
- Marissa: customer-facing one‑page summary and call scheduling with procurement/security contacts
- Rishi: confirm whether we can offer SIEM-forward logs as a push integration (yes/no, ETA) and confirm default log retention enforcement points
- Monica (Legal): prepare the sample BAA for external delivery and flag any non‑standard clauses likely to be pushed back (data destruction timelines, subcontractor disclosure cadence)

Attach: Redwood_Northvale_HIPAA_RFI_answers_v1.pdf

Thanks — I’ll prep the response bundle for Ellen once we have legal signoff.

—Kimberly

Subject: Re: Northvale RFP: HIPAA + PHI Handling Questionnaire

Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft answers. A few clarifying items before we move to contract: 

1) Data deletion & proof: We need explicit contractual language and an operational process for deletion of PHI and request traces. Can you confirm the SLA for deletion after contract termination and whether you provide deletion certificates or logs showing object removal?

2) Training data: Please confirm that customer prompts, content, or outputs are not used to improve or retrain any models unless we explicitly opt in. We need this as a checkbox in the BAA.

3) Subprocessors: Please provide the full list and the frequency of updates (we need to know how often you notify customers of new subprocessors).

4) SIEM / logging: We require either a direct push to our SIEM or a secure export that we can pull nightly. Can Redwood support an outbound push (syslog/HTTPS) into a customer-managed collector?

5) Pen tests & vulnerability disclosure: We require summary findings from last 12 months and proof of remediation timelines.

Also — please attach a sample BAA that we can share internally. If possible, schedule a call Apr 6 or 7 with your security and legal to walk the doc.

Thanks,
Ellen Brown
Lead, Security Sourcing
Northvale Health

Ellen — thanks for the follow ups. Please find attached: Redwood_BAA_Sample_2025.pdf and Appendix-Technical-Evidence.zip (SOC 2 excerpt, pen test summary, subprocessors list). Below are concise responses to your items: 

1) Deletion & proof: We provide contract language for data deletion and will execute deletion within 30 calendar days of contract termination for customer data stored in our control plane. For Dedicated and Private deployments, customer data resides in tenant-controlled resources — deletion processes are documented and can be validated by providing object-deletion logs or hash lists on request. We can include a deletion certificate appendice (standard) in the BAA.

2) Training data: Redwood does NOT use customer prompts, content, or outputs to train or fine-tune public models unless the customer explicitly opts in. This opt-in clause is included in the attached BAA sample.

3) Subprocessors: Appendix includes current subprocessors (AWS — compute/storage; GCP — storage archive; Datadog — monitoring; Fastly — edge CDN). We publish updates to the subprocessors list quarterly and provide advance notice for material changes; emergency additions are disclosed as soon as feasible per the contract.

4) SIEM / logging: We support outbound log delivery options: syslog/HTTPS push to a customer collector, S3 export, or direct SIEM integration (Splunk/Datadog) for Dedicated/Private customers. We'll work with your security team to configure an encrypted delivery channel and confirm mutual auth details.

5) Pen tests & vuln disclosure: Summary of the last external penetration test is in the appendix; remediation timelines were within 45 days for critical findings and are included in the report. We maintain a vulnerability disclosure program and will provide a contact for coordinated disclosure.

Next steps:
- Attached: Redwood_BAA_Sample_2025.pdf (editable), Appendix-Technical-Evidence.zip
- Request: please confirm preferred meeting time Apr 6 or Apr 7 and list your legal/security attendees.

If Northvale expects PHI to be processed at scale, we recommend evaluating Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private (VPC/on‑prem) as the primary deployment option — happy to run a joint technical + procurement call to align on architecture and pricing.

Best regards,
